subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What exact measurement environment, runbook scope, and acceptance criteria should count as done for this constrained-VPS reasoning-latency analysis?
rationale: The issue is valid but broad; automation cannot safely choose whether the outcome should be a docs-only runbook, new instrumentation, live VPS benchmark evidence, or a set of follow-up optimization issues without maintainer intent.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Publish a bounded native-Linux Gateway performance runbook that maps existing signals to each requested layer and identifies measured gaps for follow-up PRs.

options.title: Wait for narrow PRs
options.body: Leave this issue open until the related prep-yield, bundle-MCP diagnostics, and bootstrap-context stall PRs either land or close, then reassess the remaining analysis gap.

options.title: Close as too broad
options.body: Close this issue only if maintainers decide broad performance investigations should not be tracked in the OpenClaw issue queue without a reproducible benchmark target.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Publish a bounded native-Linux Gateway performance runbook that maps existing signals to each requested layer and identifies measured gaps for follow-up PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main blame and docs history route most of the affected diagnostics, context, VPS, and OpenTelemetry surfaces through this owner signal.
